status.panicHint: Turn off all network simulation and fault injection

dashboard.title: Overview
dashboard.intro: Aggregated requests over the recent window. Requests touched by the simulator are counted separately.

network.title: Network Simulation
network.intro: Simulate a poor link: slow, jittery, dropping. The client sees network problems, not server errors.
network.offlineHint: Kills the connection outright. The client gets a connection reset, not an HTTP 503 — those two require completely different client code.
network.jitterHint: Randomly adds or subtracts this much, so timings stop being predictable
network.bandwidthHint: Kilobits per second (carrier convention). 0 means unlimited.
network.packetLossHint: Whole-packet loss, which shows up as a dropped connection

faults.title: Fault Injection
faults.intro: Simulate the server or the files themselves going wrong. Stacks with network simulation, e.g. "weak link + mid-download abort".
faults.empty: No rules yet. Click "Add rule", or pick a ready-made scenario from Presets.
faults.orderHint: When several rules match, only the first one in the list takes effect.
faults.matchPathGlobHint: * matches within one segment, ** crosses directories, ? matches one char. e.g. /assets/**/*.ab
faults.matchPlatformHint: Matches the first segment of /assets/{platform}/ in the URL
faults.bodyPlaceholder: Leave empty for the default message
faults.maxHitsHint: 0 means unlimited. Set to 2 for "fail twice, then succeed" to exercise retry logic.

typeHints.status: The server returns an error code directly, for testing error handling and fallbacks.
typeHints.timeout: The server ignores you entirely. The client must set its own timeout or it hangs forever.
typeHints.slowHeader: Headers arrive very late, for telling connect timeouts apart from read timeouts.
typeHints.abort: The connection is killed partway through. This is the key scenario for testing resume (Range) support.
typeHints.truncate: A full length is declared but less data is sent, then the response closes normally. Clients report a length mismatch.
typeHints.corrupt: The length is exactly right but the content is damaged. Only a client that checks md5 will notice — one that doesn't will "succeed" and blow up later at unpack or runtime.
typeHints.empty: Returns 200 with an empty body, for making sure empty files and empty manifests don't crash the client.

presets.title: Presets
presets.intro: A named bundle of network settings plus fault rules, applied in one click. Built-ins target the failures Unity hot-update clients actually hit.
presets.captureHint: Store the current network settings and fault rules as a new preset

logs.title: Live Logs
logs.intro: Every request is recorded, along with what the simulator did to it. "Dropped" means the connection was killed outright.
logs.empty: No logs yet. Make a call from API Console, or curl /api/health.

explorer.title: API Console
explorer.intro: Call the hot-update endpoints your game client uses. These are affected by the simulator — which is the whole point.
explorer.deviceIdHint: Used for gray-release grouping. Empty means not grouped.
explorer.downloadTimeout: Not finished after {s}s (likely a timeout fault)
explorer.noPlatform: No platforms yet. Run npm run sample to generate sample assets, then drop your packages into the asset directory.
explorer.selectFile: Pick a file to test downloading

favorites.title: Favorites
favorites.intro: Save frequently used requests and replay them in one click. Replay is the server calling itself, so it goes through the simulator.
favorites.empty: No favorites yet. Make a call in API Console, then save it here.

manual.title: Manual
manual.intro: Feature guide, configuration details, Unity integration sample and troubleshooting. This renders backend/public/manual.en.md; switching to Chinese loads manual.zh-CN.md. Refresh to pick up edits.
manual.missing: No manual is available for this language yet ({lang})

errors.networkDown: Cannot reach the backend — make sure the server is running
errors.backendDown: Backend is not responding — make sure it is running (npm start)
errors.timeout: No response after {s}s (likely a timeout fault rule)
errors.nameUrlRequired: Name and URL are both required
errors.disconnectedHint: Connection was killed; the client only sees a network error
